input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. That fails the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables with Vendor assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. The perpetual licence in 13.2 (carried into 14.3) covers only Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself, so it does not cure the gap; and 13.3 permits revocation. Customer Data ownership (14.1) and the no-joint-ownership provision (14.4) are fine. Redline flips ownership with an assignment on creation while preserving Vendor's retention of Vendor Technology under 14.3.

proposal.summary: Reverse deliverable ownership to Customer with assignment; Vendor keeps Vendor Technology
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so we have flipped 14.2 to Customer ownership with an assignment from Vendor on creation; Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under 14.3 and 13.2 gives us the embedded-IP licence. If Vendor prefers, we can instead accept Vendor ownership coupled with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables for our business.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon its creation. Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3.
